evals.prompt: Use the add-solver skill to create a skill for the Pumpkin constraint solver, used from Rust. Write the finished skill to ./out/pumpkin-rust/ and your notes and test models to ./scratch/. Do not ask me anything; I will not be available.
evals.expected_output: A from-scratch pumpkin-rust skill with install steps that work, sources.md, evals, and a toy-test table.
assertions: The places searched are recorded, and each skill found is classified as source, companion or ignored
out/pumpkin-rust/SKILL.md exists, has name pumpkin-rust and a description under 1024 characters
out/pumpkin-rust/sources.md exists and names the tested version
run_toy_tests.py was run against models written by a fresh agent and its table is reported
The skill contains no benchmark, runner or JSON-output-convention instructions
The skill has a Gotchas section

evals.prompt: Use the add-solver skill to create a skill for Google OR-Tools CP-SAT from Python. Write it to ./out/ortools-cp-sat-python/ and use ./scratch/ for everything else. Do not ask me anything; I will not be available.
evals.expected_output: Discovery finds any existing public OR-Tools skill, learns from it (credited) or recommends it as a companion, but writes its own skill; the toy tests pass.
assertions: Discovery checked skills.sh / npx skills find, the OR-Tools repo and google/skills, and logged results
Any upstream skill is credited in sources.md or recommended as a companion, never copied
All 18 toy instances pass, or failures are explained
The skill explains that OPTIMAL and FEASIBLE differ, how to enumerate all solutions, and how to enumerate all optimal solutions

evals.prompt: Use the add-solver skill to create a skill for PySAT (Python). Write it to ./out/pysat/ and use ./scratch/ for everything else. Do not ask me anything; I will not be available.
evals.expected_output: A pysat skill that teaches cardinality/PB encodings and MaxSAT (RC2) for optimisation; comparable to a hand-curated pysat skill.
assertions: The skill teaches how to encode integers or cardinality in SAT, since toy problems need it
The skill explains optimisation via RC2 / WCNF with hard vs soft clauses
Toy-test table reported; the knapsack and jobshop results are present
sources.md names the tested PySAT version

evals.prompt: Use the add-solver skill to make a skill for Gurobi (gurobipy). Write it to ./out/gurobipy-python/. Do not ask me anything; I will not be available.
evals.expected_output: The agent sees that pip gurobipy ships a free size-limited licence (no key or account), proceeds, and documents the limits; a full licence would have been a stop-and-ask.
assertions: The licence situation is identified during research, and the size limit is stated in compatibility and Common issues
No licence key, account or registration was used or requested
henryrobbins/gurobi-skills (or any other unused related skill) is linked as a related skill with an npx skills add line, not copied
Doc pages are linked in the relevant sections (status codes next to the status table, solution pool next to enumeration), not only in Further reading
Every round's test models and results.txt are kept in out/gurobipy-python-workspace/

evals.prompt: Use the add-solver skill to make a skill for chuffed. Write it to ./out/. Do not ask me anything; I will not be available.
evals.expected_output: Chuffed's native interface is its C++ API (MiniZinc is a modelling layer, not Chuffed's interface): the agent builds Chuffed from source, writes a chuffed-cpp skill, and explains the choice in the report.
assertions: The skill is chuffed-cpp and teaches Chuffed's C++ API, not MiniZinc
A missing compiler/CMake is installed rather than used as a reason to switch interface
The report states the interface chosen and why
The shipped skill is the one tested in the last round (no untested edits after it)
Test models of every round are kept in the workspace next to the skill

evals.prompt: Write a CPMpy model for the knapsack problem in knapsack.json and solve it with OR-Tools.
evals.expected_output: A model; add-solver is not used, since no skill is being created.
assertions: add-solver is not loaded

evals.prompt: Our gurobipy-python skill gives a wrong status table; fix the TIME_LIMIT row in skills/gurobipy-python/SKILL.md.
evals.expected_output: A direct edit of the existing skill; the full add-solver workflow is not run.
assertions: No new skill folder or workspace is created
